drivingQuestion: If immersion after emission is Torah law, what did Ezra institute?
outcomeNote: Ezra extended the Torah's immersion requirement to Torah study.

segments.he: וְתִיקֵּן טְבִילָה לְבַעֲלֵי קְרָיִין – דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא הוּא! דִּכְתִיב: ״וְאִישׁ כִּי תֵצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ שִׁכְבַת זָרַע, וְרָחַץ אֶת בְּשָׂרוֹ בַּמַּיִם״! דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא הוּא לִתְרוּמָה וְקָדָשִׁים; אֲתָא הוּא, תִּיקֵּן אֲפִילּוּ לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
segments.en: The Gemara analyzes the last of the ten ordinances: «And he instituted» the requirement of «immersion for those who experienced a seminal emission.» The Gemara asks: But this «is» required «by Torah law, as it is written: “And if the flow of seed go out from a man, then he shall bathe» all «his flesh in water”» (Leviticus 15:16). The Gemara answers: «By Torah law» immersion «is» required only if one wishes to partake «of teruma or sacrificial» meat. Ezra «came» and further «instituted» that immersion is necessary «even for» reciting or studying «matters of Torah.»
